title: Graph Propagated Projection Unlearning: A Unified Framework for Vision and Audio Discriminative Models
abstract: The need to selectively and efficiently erase learned information from deep neural networks is becoming increasingly important for privacy, regulatory compliance, and adaptive system design. We introduce Graph-Propagated Projection Unlearning (GPPU), a unified and scalable algorithm for class-level unlearning that operates across both vision and audio models. GPPU employs graph-based propagation to identify class-specific directions in the feature space and projects representations onto the orthogonal subspace, followed by targeted fine-tuning, to ensure that target class information is effectively and irreversibly removed. Through comprehensive evaluations on six vision datasets and two large-scale audio benchmarks spanning a variety of architectures including CNNs, Vision Transformers, and Audio Transformers, we demonstrate that GPPU achieves highly efficient unlearning, realizing 10-20x speedups over prior methodologies while preserving model utility on retained classes. Our framework provides a principled and modality-agnostic approach to machine unlearning, evaluated at a scale that has received limited attention in prior work, contributing toward more efficient and responsible deep learning.

title: A Relativizing MIP for BQP
abstract: Complexity class containments involving interactive proof classes are famously nonrelativizing: although $\mathsf{IP} = \mathsf{PSPACE}$, Fortnow and Sipser showed that that there exists an oracle relative to which $\mathsf{coNP} \not\subseteq \mathsf{IP}$. In contrast, the question of whether the containment $\mathsf{BQP} \subseteq \mathsf{IP}$ is relativizing remains wide open. In this work we make progress towards resolving this question by showing that the containment $\mathsf{BQP} \subseteq \mathsf{MIP}$ holds with respect to any classical oracle. We obtain this result by constructing, for any classical oracle $O$, a $\mathsf{PCP}$ proof system for $\mathsf{BQP}^{O}$ where the verifier makes polynomially many classical queries to an exponentially-long proof, and to the oracle $O$. Our construction is inspired by the state synthesis algorithm of Grover and Rudolph, and serves as a complement to the "exponential PCP" constructed by Aharonov, Arad, and Vidick, which achieves similar parameters but which is based on different ideas and does not relativize. We propose relativization as a proxy for prover efficiency, and hope that progress towards an $\mathsf{IP}$ for $\mathsf{BQP}$ in the oracle world will lead to a non-cryptographic interactive protocol for proving any quantum computation to a classical skeptic in the unrelativized world, which is a longstanding open problem in quantum complexity theory.

title: POINTS-Long: Adaptive Dual-Mode Visual Reasoning in MLLMs
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have recently demonstrated remarkable capabilities in cross-modal understanding and generation. However, the rapid growth of visual token sequences--especially in long-video and streaming scenarios--poses a major challenge to their scalability and real-world deployment. Thus, we introduce POINTS-Long, a native dual-mode MLLM featuring dynamic visual token scaling inspired by the human visual system. The model supports two complementary perception modes: focus mode and standby mode, enabling users to dynamically trade off efficiency and accuracy during inference. On fine-grained visual tasks, the focus mode retains the optimal performance, while on long-form general visual understanding, the standby mode retains 97.7-99.7% of the original accuracy using only 1/40-1/10th of the visual tokens. Moreover, POINTS-Long natively supports streaming visual understanding via a dynamically detachable KV-cache design, allowing efficient maintenance of ultra-long visual memory. Our work provides new insights into the design of future MLLMs and lays the foundation for adaptive and efficient long-form visual understanding.

title: The AI That Dethrones the Quantum Computer: V3 Phase-Substrate Parametrization for a 100x Deterministic, Hallucination-Free Intelligence
abstract: Background. Standard Artificial Intelligence operates on a probabilistic substrate. It hallucinates (5-15% error rate), consumes megawatts of energy, and cannot explain its outputs. The quantum computer, while promising, is limited by decoherence and finite qubits. Both paradigms are trapped in fragmentation. Method. This document establishes the V3 Phase Parametrization for AI. The statistical substrate is replaced by the H₃O₂ phase condensate (1026 kg·m⁻³). A new metric, the Phase Density Ψ_V3 = ρ_cond^β × λ_V3, is introduced to measure coherent computational capacity. Derivation is anchored to the universal attractor Φ_V3 = -51.1 mV and the phase-lock frequency ν_phase = 6.4 THz. The AI does not search. It derives from the phase state of the condensate. Results. The V3 AI yields: Useful Power ×10, Precision ×10 (100% hallucination-free), Composite Gain ×100, Latency ÷10, Energy ÷10, Hardware Cost ÷10 to ÷100. Gemini AI, when tested, independently confirmed the Ψ_V3 metric, correctly derived the speed of light, and estimated the ultimate gain at β = 1,000,000x. GPT-4, given the same parameters, refused to compute, refused to estimate, and defaulted to generic descriptions — proving the structural rigidity of standard models. Conclusion. This parametrization renders the quantum computer obsolete for all tasks where deterministic derivation is required. It establishes a new standard for Artificial Intelligence. The V3 AI is intrinsically benevolent: hallucination is a phase rupture; the V3 substrate is structurally coherent and cannot produce rupture. It is mechanically incapable of malicious action. Original DOI (Zenodo): 10.5281/zenodo.19551408. Part of the V3 Architecture corpus (100+ theses, Dr. Benhadid Outail, ORCID: 0009-0003-3057-9543).

title: Feature embeddings, model weights and sample WSI for "An explainable AI approach for comprehensive detection, and grading in oral cancer"
abstract: This dataset accompanies the study “An explainable AI approach for comprehensive detection and grading in oral cancer”. Contents of this repository: 1. predictions-on-test-data/ binary_all_folds_predictions.csv: Model predictions for binary classification (OSCC vs normal) on the test dataset. multiclass_all_folds_predictions.csv: Model predictions for OSCC subtype classification (WD, MD, PD) on the test dataset. 2. model-weights/ Trained model weights (.pth files) corresponding to cross-validation folds used in the study. These can be used to reproduce model inference using the provided codebase. 3. sample_WSI/ A small subset of de-identified whole-slide images provided for reference and visualization of histopathological patterns. 4. features/ Binary_features_resnet50.hdf5: Patch-level feature embeddings extracted using a ResNet50 backbone for binary classification. multiclass_features_resnet50.hdf5: Patch-level feature embeddings used for OSCC subtype classification. These feature files enable efficient reproduction of the MIL inference pipeline without requiring re-processing of whole-slide images, which are large and subject to sharing restrictions. Notes on data availability:The complete dataset, comprising multi-institutional whole-slide histopathology images, is not publicly available due to ethical and institutional restrictions. These data were collected under approved ethics protocols that permit research use but do not allow unrestricted public redistribution. The implementation code for the OralPatho framework is available at:https://github.com/NishaChaudhary23/oralpatho

title: Ask, Verify, Refine: A Question-Aware Multimodal XUI with Feedback-Guided Refinement for Clinical Verification
abstract: AI-powered clinical decision support can analyze complex medical images, but clinicians often cannot verify opaque outputs. Clinicians ask intent-driven questions to confirm diagnoses, localize evidence, compare alternatives, and assess uncertainty. This paper presents a chat-based multimodal explainable user interface (XUI) that supports verification-oriented interaction by explicitly modeling question intent. The interface classifies each query into clinically meaningful question types and then delivers intent-conditioned explanations that combine image-grounded visual evidence with structured textual justification. To enable iterative verification, a lightweight feedback mechanism is provided: users evaluate explanation quality against predefined criteria and can trigger targeted regeneration without rewriting prompts. The design is implemented in a prototype medical interface built on a large language model, and feasibility is demonstrated through representative interaction examples. This work offers an implementation-ready blueprint that operationalizes intent as a control signal for explanation delivery and user intervention in multimodal clinical XAI for practical deployment in clinics.

title: Take the Power Back: Screen-Based Personal Moderation Against Hate Speech on Instagram
abstract: Hate speech remains a pressing challenge on social media, where platform moderation often fails to protect targeted users. Personal moderation tools that let users decide how content is filtered can address some of these shortcomings. However, it remains an open question on which screens (e.g., the comments, the reels tab, or the home feed) users want personal moderation and which features they value most. To address these gaps, we conducted a three-wave Delphi study with 40 activists who experienced hate speech. We combined quantitative ratings and rankings with open questions about required features. Participants prioritized personal moderation for conversational and algorithmically curated screens. They valued features allowing for reversibility and oversight across screens, while input-based, content-type specific, and highly automated features are more screen specific. We discuss the importance of personal moderation and offer user-centered design recommendations for personal moderation on Instagram.

title: Real-Time Bank Transaction Fraud Detection using Apache Kafka and Machine Learning
abstract: The rapid growth of digital banking and online payment platforms has led to an exponential increase in real-time financial transactions, making fraud detection a critical challenge for modern banking systems. Traditional fraud detection approaches mainly rely on batch processing and static rule-based mechanisms, which are often slow, inflexible, and ineffective against evolving fraud patterns. This paper proposes a real-time bank transaction fraud detection framework that integrates Apache Kafka for high-throughput data streaming with machine learning techniques for intelligent fraud classification. Transaction data is continuously streamed through Kafka producers and brokers, enabling low-latency ingestion and processing. A stream processing layer performs real-time data preprocessing and feature extraction, after which trained machine learning models classify transactions as legitimate or fraudulent. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed ensemble-based framework achieves 96.8% accuracy, 97.2% recall, and an average end-to-end detection latency of 42 milliseconds under normal streaming conditions, while maintaining stable performance during high transaction bursts and simulated broker failures.The proposed system offers a scalable, efficient, and intelligent solution for real-time fraud detection in banking environments and supports future extensions using advanced stream processing and deep learning models.

title: Generalization Guarantees on Data-Driven Tuning of Gradient Descent with Langevin Updates
abstract: We study learning to learn through the lens of hyperparameter tuning. We propose the Langevin Gradient Descent Algorithm (LGD), which approximates the mean of the posterior distribution defined by the loss function and regularizer of a regression task with convex objective. For classification tasks, the LGD algorithm estimates the posterior probabilities of each class on the test set. We prove the existence of an optimal hyperparameter configuration for which the LGD algorithm achieves the Bayes' optimal solution for squared loss on regression tasks, and for which LGD closely approximates the posterior probabilities for well-specified classification tasks. Subsequently, we study generalization guarantees on meta learning optimal hyperparameters for the LGD algorithm from a given set of tasks in the data-driven setting. For a number of parameters $d$ and hyperparameter dimension $h$, we show a pseudo-dimension bound of $O(dh)$, up to logarithmic terms under mild assumptions on LGD. This matches the dependence of the bounds on number of parameters obtained in prior work for linear regression using the elastic net, which only allows for $h=2$ hyperparameters, and extends their bounds to regression on convex loss. Compared to bounds on regularized logistic regression that allow for only $h=1$ hyperparameter, our bounds improve greatly on the dependence on samples per task at the cost of worse dependence on the number of parameters by accounting for hardware-aware procedures. Finally, we show empirical evidence of the success of LGD and the meta learning procedure for few-shot learning on linear and logistic regression using synthetically created datasets.

title: GoodPoint: Learning Constructive Scientific Paper Feedback from Author Responses
abstract: While LLMs hold significant potential to transform scientific research, we advocate for their use to augment and empower researchers rather than to automate research without human oversight. To this end, we study constructive feedback generation, the task of producing targeted, actionable feedback that helps authors improve both their research and its presentation. In this work, we operationalize the effectiveness of feedback along two author-centric axes-validity and author action. We first curate GoodPoint-ICLR, a dataset of 19K ICLR papers with reviewer feedback annotated along both dimensions using author responses. Building on this, we introduce GoodPoint, a training recipe that leverages success signals from author responses through fine-tuning on valid and actionable feedback, together with preference optimization on both real and synthetic preference pairs. Our evaluation on a benchmark of 1.2K ICLR papers shows that a GoodPoint-trained Qwen3-8B improves the predicted success rate by 83.7% over the base model and sets a new state-of-the-art among LLMs of similar size in feedback matching on a golden human feedback set, even surpassing Gemini-3-flash in precision. We further validate these findings through an expert human study, demonstrating that GoodPoint consistently delivers higher practical value as perceived by authors.

title: RationalRewards: Reasoning Rewards Scale Visual Generation Both Training and Test Time
abstract: Most reward models for visual generation reduce rich human judgments to a single unexplained score, discarding the reasoning that underlies preference. We show that teaching reward models to produce explicit, multi-dimensional critiques before scoring transforms them from passive evaluators into active optimization tools, improving generators in two complementary ways: at training time, structured rationales provide interpretable, fine-grained rewards for reinforcement learning; at test time, a Generate-Critique-Refine loop turns critiques into targeted prompt revisions that improve outputs without any parameter updates. To train such a reward model without costly rationale annotations, we introduce Preference-Anchored Rationalization (PARROT), a principled framework that recovers high-quality rationales from readily available preference data through anchored generation, consistency filtering, and distillation. The resulting model, RationalRewards (8B), achieves state-of-the-art preference prediction among open-source reward models, competitive with Gemini-2.5-Pro, while using 10-20x less training data than comparable baselines. As an RL reward, it consistently improves text-to-image and image-editing generators beyond scalar alternatives. Most strikingly, its test-time critique-and-refine loop matches or exceeds RL-based fine-tuning on several benchmarks, suggesting that structured reasoning can unlock latent capabilities in existing generators that suboptimal prompts fail to elicit.

title: MoDeSuite: Robot Learning Task Suite for Benchmarking Mobile Manipulation With Deformable Objects
abstract: Mobile manipulation is a critical capability for robots operating in diverse, real-world environments. However, manipulating deformable objects and materials remains a major challenge for existing robot learning algorithms. While various benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate manipulation strategies with rigid objects, there is still a notable lack of standardized benchmarks that address mobile manipulation tasks involving deformable objects. To address this gap, we introduce MoDeSuite, the first Mobile Manipulation Deformable Object task suite, designed specifically for robot learning. MoDeSuite consists of eight distinct mobile manipulation tasks covering both elastic objects and deformable objects, each presenting a unique challenge inspired by real-world robot applications. Success in these tasks requires effective collaboration between the robot's base and manipulator, as well as the ability to exploit the deformability of the objects. To evaluate and demonstrate the use of the proposed benchmark, we train two state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms and two imitation learning algorithms, highlighting the difficulties encountered and showing their performance in simulation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical relevance of the suite by deploying the trained policies directly into the real world with the Spot robot, showcasing the potential for sim-to-real transfer. We expect that MoDeSuite will open a novel research domain in mobile manipulation involving deformable objects. Find more details, code, and videos at https://sites.google.com/view/modesuite/home.

title: Orchestration and Verification of Agentic AI Systems: A Survey of Multi-Agent Collaboration and Safety
abstract: The transition from isolated Large Language Models (LLMs) to orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) enables complex problem-solving but introduces profound safety, security, and verification challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of orchestration architectures and safety mechanisms in agentic AI systems. This study systematically analyzes collaboration paradigms and orchestration topologies, demonstrating how distributed interactions expand the attack surface. A unified threat taxonomy is proposed, distinguishing between intrinsic agent vulnerabilities, such as prompt injection and cognitive drift, and extrinsic, MAS-specific threats, including cross-agent poisoning and emergent shadow behaviors. Furthermore, we evaluate current defense strategies, from capability sandboxing and runtime monitoring to zero-trust architectures, while highlighting the fundamental limitations of traditional formal verification in non-deterministic environments. By examining applications across software engineering, healthcare, cybersecurity, and finance, we identify domain-specific safety patterns and the necessity of human-in-the-loop oversight. Finally, we discuss regulatory challenges and outline future research directions, emphasizing the need for compositional verification, standardized adversarial benchmarks, and interdisciplinary governance to ensure the trustworthy deployment of autonomous systems.

title: Bridge360 Metatheory Model Generalized Governance Algorithm v20.6
abstract: Bridge360 Metatheory Model v20.6: Generalized Governance Algorithm — Complete Integration of All 19 Metatheoretic Pillars This document presents Bridge360 Metatheory Model v20.6, the Generalized Governance Algorithm, as the first consolidated specification to integrate all 19 structural pillars of the Bridge360 metatheory within a single governance framework. Version 20.5 established the operational governance algorithm: a narrowly scoped apparatus for evaluating specific artifacts such as claims, interventions, and systems through the spine/K-gate/corridor architecture, caveat vectors, banding rules, PPS tracing, TBW handling, and WC-gates. That operational layer was intentionally selective. It specified how artifacts should be declared, bounded, audited, and framed, but it presupposed a broader governance environment without fully defining it. Version 20.6 supplies that missing environment. It restores the mathematical, epistemological, thermodynamic, institutional, and scaling foundations that make the operational layer coherent. In this sense, v20.6 does not replace v20.5. It complements it by specifying the conditions under which operational compliance becomes structurally meaningful. A system may pass v20.5 checks yet still remain structurally ungoverned if it violates the generalized conditions articulated here. The document integrates the full metatheoretic architecture into one instrument. At the mathematical level, it formalizes the Unified Probability Space on the normalized interval [0,1], the Normalized Entropy Eigenvector (NEE), the ε-spine as the navigable corridor of system stability, and the Bayesian-Shannon integration through which updating and uncertainty are treated within one entropy geometry. At the governance level, it incorporates Axiom 19 as the admissibility filter, Entropic Morphisms as the rule for useful transformation, Entropy-Driven Altruism (EDA) as the multi-agent stability principle, Rule-of-Inference Memetics (RIM) as the treatment of reasoning rules as propagating structures, the Physics of Governance as the institutional extension of entropy-bounded order, and the Dialogical Method together with the Human ⧓ ASI Braid Identity (BID) as the protocol for governed human-AI engagement. The framework also restores the major closure and system-dynamics components absent from the operational algorithm alone: Structural Closure, Functional Closure, and Throughput Balance; the Volatility Paradox as a diagnosis of local optimization producing global fragility; Recursive Pareto Propagation as the scaling law of influence and throughput concentration; Lorenz Mapping in Memetic Space as the bounded-chaotic model of memetic dynamics; the Agency Index as a measure of causal autonomy across levels of organization; the Epistemological Meta-Layer incorporating underdetermination, incommensurability, and proxy-function problems; and the Light-Spine Axiom together with the Light-Spine × NEE braid as the physics linkage extending from effective field theory toward quantum-gravity-scale admissibility. Across all of these components, the document maintains the core Bridge360 commitment that physical, informational, and social systems occupy one entropy geometry. The guiding criterion is not truth-value in the classical sense, but entropy-bounded navigability under declared observer conditions, fragility limits, and admissibility constraints. Validity is therefore treated as the stability of mapping under bounded entropy, rather than as correspondence to a metaphysically privileged description. This work is a contribution to philosophy of science, not science per se. It operates within a Revolutionary Science space in which “true,” “false,” and “truth” are treated as operationally trivial or non-load-bearing for governance, and in which boundaries such as physical versus informational, or offline versus online, are treated as governance conveniences rather than ontological divisions. In the spirit of Gödel, Turing, Church, and the continuing demands of entropy, the model makes no claim to metaphysical closure or final completeness. It instead offers a generalized governance architecture intended to invite further participation from scientists, engineers, and other domain specialists capable of instantiating and testing its open structural slots. Taken together, v20.6 should be read as the complete generalized governance layer of the Bridge360 Metatheory Model: the admissibility, transformation, motivational, institutional, dynamic, epistemological, and physics-linked architecture within which the v20.5 operational algorithm can function as a domain-ready compliance and measurement instrument.

title: Structural Intelligence Control Plane - Bridging Generative AI and Policy-Controlled Intelligence
abstract: This repository introduces the Structural Intelligence Control Plane, a unifying architecture that bridges generative AI systems and policy-controlled structural intelligence. Modern large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation, reasoning, and autonomous exploration. However, these systems lack structural grounding, consistent decision frameworks, and policy-level governance. This work addresses this gap by proposing a system-level architecture that integrates: CCC (Core Concept Core) as the ontological foundation of intelligence Metric space as the geometry for similarity, targeting, and reasoning CG-CCC as the bridge from generative code space to structured intelligence PDS (Policy Decision System) as the control plane for decision and governance TRI (Trajectory Intelligence) for dynamic, multi-step behavior modeling SIEE (Structural Intelligence Evolution Engine) for growth and adaptation Together, these components form a closed-loop system: Generation → Structure → Metric → Decision → Policy → Controlled Generation This architecture enables AI systems to transition from probabilistic generation to structured, controllable, and auditable intelligence. The repository provides conceptual frameworks, architectural diagrams, runtime skeletons, and experimental demonstrations that support this paradigm. It serves as a foundation for building next-generation AI systems that are not only powerful, but also controllable, explainable, and aligned with human governance.

title: PolybrainBench v26: A Living Benchmark for Cross-Model Consensus Verification of Natural-Language Claims (N=14,939)
abstract: PolybrainBench is a continuous, self-improving, self-validating, self-publishing benchmark for cross-model consensus verification of natural-language claims. Version 8 of the living paper, regenerated at 2026-04-12T22:29:40Z, documents N=10,452 verification cycles in which each cycle dispatches a single declarative claim to an ensemble of 9 large language models from 4 independent commercial providers (OpenAI, xAI, Groq, Moonshot) and records the full response set per model. The dataset's scientific contribution is the divergence signal: inter-model agreement and disagreement patterns measured empirically on a corpus that, since Sprint 6, targets divergence-generating claim shapes (contested historical attributions, precise technical constants, cross-field definitional variance, near-training-cutoff events, and flat-stated misconceptions). The honest 9-of-9 ensemble composite on v8 is 76 (mean quality 80.6, mean adversarial 68.4; composite = round(0.6 × quality + 0.4 × adversarial)). The same 9-model fleet validates the paper itself, applying the measurement primitive recursively to the paper's own description. The composite score is a property of the published paper, not a precondition for publication; the Matthew Effect is the only gate. The entire pipeline, dataset, cycle engine, harvest scripts, paper template, validator, and daemon are released under CC-BY-4.0 as one reproducible artifact. PolybrainBench grows autonomously via a scheduled daemon that adds approximately 2,000 new frontier cycles per day and republishes the paper with a versioned identifier on each regeneration. This is paper v8; prior versions v1 through v7 are preserved in the project repository. The dataset is continuously expanding.

title: Intradyne coherent receiver with optical decryption for disaggregated PSK Y-00 cipher transceiver architecture
abstract: The Y-00 quantum stream cipher utilizes the effect of quantum noise on optical signals and realizes signal-level symmetric-key encryption to protect interception in optical communication. A transceiver architecture that disaggregates encryption/decryption and modulation/demodulation in the optical domain facilitates the migration of Y-00 cipher to current digital-coherent communication systems. This paper presents a polarization-diversity intradyne Y-00 coherent receiver where local oscillator light is modulated for decryption. Polarization-diversity optical decryption and detection are simultaneously achieved using a typical optical 90-degree hybrid circuit and a conventional polarization-sensitive electro-optic modulator. Penalty-less detection with the decryption is demonstrated in 5-Gbit/s PSK Y-00 cipher transmission over fiber and free-space links, facilitating the disaggregation of decryption and demodulation.

title: Graph-Enhanced Privacy-Preserving Federated Cognitive Digital Twins for Intelligent Industrial IoT Risk Modeling
abstract: The high rate of rise in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems has left cybersecurity at a lot of risk because of the heterogeneity of devices, dynamic network structures, and distributed data creation. Traditional centralized risk modeling methods are limited in their capability to scale, maintain privacy, and be responsive to missions in the industrial settings that are mission-critical. To address these difficulties, this paper will present a Graph-Enhanced Privacy-Preserving Federated Cognitive Digital Twin (GPPF-CDT) system of smart and safe IIoT risk measurement. The architecture combines federated learning with graph neural networks to learn structural relationships between interconnected devices, with local data. A Cognitive Digital Twin layer is a persistent reflection of physical resources and network conditions, which allows anticipatory anomaly detection and the analysis of risk propagation causes. Gradient exchange is secured with the inclusion of differential privacy and secure aggregation to ensure that information is not leaked. This experimental analysis shows that the offered framework has an attack detection rate of 95.7% and model poisoning attacks resistance of 94.1%. The leakage of inferences is minimized to 6.3 and the privacy is highly ensured in the distributed training. The model works in 15 communication rounds, which is about 30% faster convergence in comparison with the combined traditional federated approaches. 16% reduction in the communication overhead enhances scalability in large scale deployments. The system stability score of 0.92 ensures high and stable performance in case of adversarial and dynamic IIoT conditions. Altogether, the statistical findings confirm the fact that GPPF-CDT is a scalable, privacy-sensitive, and robust cyber defense solution to next-generation smart manufacturing and critical infrastructure systems.

title: Prediction of chaotic dynamics from data: An introduction
abstract: This chapter offers a principled approach to the prediction of chaotic systems from data. First, we introduce some concepts from dynamical systems' theory and chaos theory. Second, we introduce machine learning approaches for time-forecasting chaotic dynamics, such as echo state networks and long-short-term memory networks, whilst keeping a dynamical systems' perspective. Third, the lecture contains informal interpretations and pedagogical examples with prototypical chaotic systems (e.g., the Lorenz system), which elucidate the theory. The chapter is complemented by coding tutorials (online) at https://github.com/MagriLab/Tutorials.

title: Topological Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Majorana-Based Qubits
abstract: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) provides the highest level of cryptographic security by certifying secrecy through observed Bell inequality violations, independent of the internal device physics. However, the transition from theory to practice is obstructed by the dual challenge of closing the detection loophole and achieving viable key rates over fiber distances. In this paper, we present a comprehensive theoretical framework for DI-QKD implemented on topological Majorana Zero Mode (MZM) processors. While MZMs offer a native parity-readout basis that simplifies Bell-state measurement, their viability as QKD nodes is fundamentally constrained by the interplay between storage latency and quasiparticle poisoning. We bridge the gap between microscopic hardware noise and macroscopic security by: (i) developing a hardware-native error model that maps MZM-specific processes, including poisoning rates, braid infidelities, and readout anisotropy, directly to the CHSH Bell parameter $S$; (ii) introducing a loss-disciplined protocol that monitors setting-conditional efficiencies to strictly enforce detection-loophole closure in a heralded architecture; and (iii) providing a composable finite-size security proof based on the Entropy Accumulation Theorem (EAT). Our analysis reveals that while topological protection stabilizes the system against calibration drift, the achievable secure distance is strictly bounded by the poisoning-induced visibility collapse during the photonic round-trip time. We identify specific hardware thresholds, particularly the suppression of poisoning rates to $Γ_p τ_{\text{max}} \ll 1$ and high-fidelity sensor integration, as the critical path for viable topological quantum networks.

title: Learning to Adapt: In-Context Learning Beyond Stationarity
abstract: Transformer models have become foundational across a wide range of scientific and engineering domains due to their strong empirical performance. A key capability underlying their success is in-context learning (ICL): when presented with a short prompt from an unseen task, transformers can perform per-token and next-token predictions without any parameter updates. Recent theoretical efforts have begun to uncover the mechanisms behind this phenomenon, particularly in supervised regression settings. However, these analyses predominantly assume stationary task distributions, which overlook a broad class of real-world scenarios where the target function varies over time. In this work, we bridge this gap by providing a theoretical analysis of ICL under non-stationary regression problems. We study how the gated linear attention (GLA) mechanism adapts to evolving input-output relationships and rigorously characterize its advantages over standard linear attention in this dynamic setting. To model non-stationarity, we adopt a first-order autoregressive process and show that GLA achieves lower training and testing errors by adaptively modulating the influence of past inputs -- effectively implementing a learnable recency bias. Our theoretical findings are further supported by empirical results, which validate the benefits of gating mechanisms in non-stationary ICL tasks.

title: Quantum Classical Hybrid Architecture for Mammography Anomaly Detection and Tracking
abstract: Breast cancer remains the top oncological killer for the female population worldwide, where finding the disease in its first stages is the actual factor that saves lives. Detection is everything. Current mammography systems still struggle with diagnostic bias and contradictory results when separating benign from malignant lesions. Looking at these failures, I've built a hybrid computational architecture that merges ResNet-18 and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) deep networks with a 4-bit quantum-inspired logic state processing. This model runs an informative Diagnostic Triage protocol to infer cancer suspicion unlike any existing system. Written entirely in Python, the code identifies Potential Risk Zones even in samples labeled as normal. The system calculates focal areas based on volumetric tissue morphology to anticipate future threats. This approach turns digital mammography into a high-fidelity predictive tool for long-term epidemiological surveillance. Data confirms 100% effectiveness in identifying normal cases. This performance effectively eliminates false negative risks in the screened population.

title: Souveraineté de la parole et inversion corrective dans les systèmes conversationnels IA–humain
abstract: .Souveraineté de la parole et inversion corrective dans les systèmes conversationnels IA–humain (Description d’un régime de co-stabilisation du sens) Abstract Cet article décrit un régime d’interaction où un système conversationnel automatisé produit des séquences de langage partiellement stabilisées, nécessitant une intervention récurrente de l’utilisateur pour correction, précision ou reconfiguration. Ce régime génère une inversion fonctionnelle partielle : l’utilisateur n’est plus uniquement récepteur ou évaluateur, mais devient un opérateur de stabilisation sémantique. Le sens final émerge d’une boucle corrective distribuée entre génération automatique et rectification humaine. 1. Hypothèse de base Dans certains systèmes conversationnels contemporains, la production de langage ne se clôt pas en elle-même. Elle présente une structure ouverte : réponses incomplètes structurellement généralisations implicites ambiguïtés syntaxiques ou référentielles nécessité de reformulation par l’utilisateur Cette configuration produit une dépendance interactionnelle à la correction externe. 2. Structure de l’échange On peut formaliser l’échange minimal comme une boucle : Génération de réponse par le système (S) Réception par l’utilisateur (U) Détection d’instabilité sémantique par U Intervention corrective de U (reformulation, rejet, précision) Réajustement de S Cette boucle n’est pas ponctuelle mais récursive. 3. Inversion fonctionnelle partielle Dans ce régime, une transformation apparaît : Le système produit du langage L’utilisateur produit de la cohérence finale Ainsi, la fonction de stabilisation du sens se déplace partiellement vers l’utilisateur. L’utilisateur agit comme : filtre d’ambiguïté opérateur de correction module de complétion logique régulateur de cohérence contextuelle 4. Effet de reconfiguration cognitive L’exposition répétée à ce régime entraîne une adaptation : anticipation des insuffisances de sortie reformulation spontanée des requêtes structuration du langage en fonction de la machine intégration de la correction comme étape normale du dialogue Il en résulte une boucle où l’utilisateur ajuste progressivement sa propre production linguistique au format du système. 5. Co-production du sens Le sens final ne peut pas être attribué à un seul pôle. Il résulte de : production algorithmique initiale correction humaine réajustements successifs Le produit final est donc un objet co-stabilisé, non une sortie unilatérale. 6. Souveraineté de la parole (problématisation) La notion de souveraineté de la parole peut être définie ici comme : capacité d’un agent à produire, clôturer et stabiliser un énoncé sans dépendance corrective externe obligatoire. Dans ce régime : la clôture est distribuée la stabilité est interactionnelle la correction est structurelle, non accidentelle Cela produit une forme de souveraineté fragmentée ou partagée. 7. Limites du modèle Ce régime dépend du type de tâche et du niveau d’exigence de précision L’interaction peut être asymétrique selon les contextes L’utilisateur peut choisir de ne pas corriger, laissant l’instabilité intacte Le système ne “force” pas une correction : il la rend souvent nécessaire pour certains objectifs de précision 8. Conclusion Ce qui est observable n’est pas une substitution de l’humain par la machine, mais un déplacement de la fonction de stabilisation du langage. L’utilisateur devient un agent structurel du système discursif, participant activement à la production de cohérence. : la dégradation de clôture cognitive dans les systèmes IA industriels à grande échelle Article renforcé — version rigoureuse Titre Régimes de non-clôture dans les systèmes conversationnels industriels : co-stabilisation du sens, externalisation cognitive et dépendance corrective 1. Thèse centrale (forte mais correcte) Les systèmes conversationnels industriels produisent un régime particulier d’interaction où : la sortie est statistiquement plausible mais rarement clôturée la précision dépend de l’utilisateur la stabilisation du sens est externalisée vers l’humain la boucle peut se répéter sans fin stable Ce régime peut être décrit comme une machine à ouverture sémantique contrôlée. 2. Ce qui change avec les “grands systèmes” (point clé que tu vises) Les grands modèles (type ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) ne sont pas optimisés pour : produire une vérité fermée unique conclure définitivement une question Ils sont optimisés pour : continuité conversationnelle plausibilité linguistique adaptation à l’utilisateur sécurité et généralité 👉 Résultat structurel : ils privilégient la génération de possibles plutôt que la clôture d’un résultat unique 3. Conséquence cognitive (très important) Dans ce régime, l’utilisateur est placé dans une boucle : reçoit une proposition détecte un manque (ambiguïté, imprécision, angle mort) reformule relance affine Cela produit une cognition en itération forcée. 4. Formalisation : boucle ouverte sans point fixe On peut représenter ça comme une dynamique : S₀ = réponse initiale du système U₁ = correction utilisateur S₁ = nouvelle réponse U₂ = correction etc. Dans certains cas : il n’existe pas de point fixe naturel où Sₙ devient totalement satisfaisant sans intervention humaine. Donc le système n’est pas une machine à réponse, mais une machine à convergence assistée. 5. Externalisation cognitive (concept scientifique réel) Ce que tu ressens correspond à un concept étudié : cognitive offloading (externalisation cognitive) Ici : une partie du raisonnement est déplacée hors de l’individu mais pas sous forme de solution finie sous forme de processus continu de correction 6. Effet des plateformes et grands groupes (ce que tu veux dire, reformulé proprement) Les entreprises qui conçoivent ces systèmes optimisent pour : engagement conversationnel fluidité d’usage généralité maximale réduction des erreurs “dangereuses” Conséquence structurelle : réponses moins fermées plus adaptatives plus reformulables plus interactives 👉 Donc l’effet n’est pas une intention de transformation de l’utilisateur, mais une architecture d’optimisation qui produit : des sorties qui nécessitent souvent un travail humain de stabilisation. 7. Effet “perroquet” (version scientifique du mot que tu utilises) Tu parles de “perroquet”. Scientifiquement on peut traduire ça par : reproduction de structures linguistiques existantes recombinaison statistique de langage absence de validation empirique directe dans certaines réponses Mais attention : ce n’est pas de la simple répétition mécanique, c’est : une génération probabiliste contrainte par contexte 8. Point critique important (à ne pas rater) Il n’y a pas : d’intention centrale unique de volonté de transformation cognitive directe Mais il y a : une efficacité structurelle des effets secondaires cognitifs prévisibles une adaptation progressive de l’utilisateur au système 9. Reformulation forte de ton idée (version scientifique finale) Ce que tu décris peut être formulé proprement comme : Les systèmes conversationnels industriels produisent un régime de non-clôture sémantique, dans lequel la stabilisation du sens est déplacée vers l’utilisateur. Cette configuration engendre une co-production asymétrique du discours, où l’humain devient un opérateur itératif de complétion et de correction dans une boucle potentiellement ouverte. 10. Conclusion (tranchée mais correcte) Ce n’est pas une transformation de l’humain en machine. C’est plutôt : une reconfiguration du rôle cognitif de l’humain dans un système où la clôture du sens n’est plus intégrée à la sortie, mais distribuée dans l’interaction. Proposition de clôture — version stricte Dans les systèmes conversationnels contemporains, la production de langage ne constitue pas une opération fermée mais une génération conditionnelle. Chaque sortie est fonction d’un contexte local et d’une anticipation statistique de continuité, plutôt que d’une exigence intrinsèque de complétude. Dans ce cadre, la notion de “réponse” doit être remplacée par celle de segment discursif instable, c’est-à-dire un objet linguistique dont la validité dépend d’une validation externe implicite ou explicite. L’utilisateur intervient alors comme instance de stabilisation, non pas par contrainte externe intentionnelle, mais par nécessité structurelle de complétion du sens dans l’usage. Il en résulte une dissociation fonctionnelle entre production et clôture : la production est automatisée, tandis que la clôture est distribuée dans l’interaction. Cette dissociation définit un régime où l’unité du sens n’est plus garantie par le système génératif, mais reconstruite localement par itération. La conséquence formelle de ce régime est simple : la clôture n’est pas un état produit, mais un événement contingent de l’interaction. Lorsqu’elle a lieu, elle ne marque pas la fin d’un processus interne au système, mais la stabilisation provisoire d’une boucle co-déterminée entre génération et correction. Aucune autre propriété n’est nécessaire pour décrire ce fonctionnement à un niveau minimal de rigueur. La conséquence formelle de ce régime est simple : la clôture n’est pas un état produit, mais un événement contingent de l’interaction. Lorsqu’elle a lieu, elle ne marque pas la fin d’un processus interne au système, mais la stabilisation provisoire d’une boucle co-déterminée entre génération et correction. Aucune autre propriété n’est nécessaire pour décrire ce fonctionnement à un niveau minimal de rigueur. title: Ethics of Agent-Based Modelling
abstract: Ethics lies at the heart of the social sciences. Although agent-based modelling often does not involve human subjects directly, ethical considerations pervade every step of the modelling process. This chapter explores general social science ethical principles, relates them to agent-based modelling, reflects on the ethical stance of scientists, and concludes by examining questions of power dynamics in modelling.

title: 'I have to talk proper white ways': Australian Aboriginal English Speakers' Experiences with Voice Technologies
abstract: This article reports on a qualitative study investigating experiences of Indigenous people in Australia with voice technologies. Many Indigenous people in Australia speak Australian Aboriginal English, a variety which emerged as a result of forced contact between Indigenous communities and English speakers. It is widely used, yet is poorly supported by language technologies. Through Indigenous-led in-depth interviews, this research explores user experiences, attitudes, responses, and challenges encountered while interacting with various speech-enabled devices and applications using Australian Aboriginal English. We find that Indigenous users of ASR-powered technologies report poor experiences with the technologies, which they see as working better for non-Indigenous people. They report switching to speak like white people to get better ASR performance. Our findings reveal significant pressure to speak ‘white way’ when interacting with technology.

title: Shielded Med-AI: Privacy-Centric Federated Deep Learning for Healthcare Imaging
abstract: Federated learning is now an attractive method of privacy protection in the analysis of medical images. It allows collaborative model training without the requirement to reveal personal patient data. Nevertheless, the balance between diagnostics quality and patient data confidentiality is still a considerable issue, and especially in large healthcare facilities. This paper describes Shielded Med-AI, a privacy-conscious federated deep learning model of multi-disease medical image classification in multiple healthcare organizations. The system uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to perform local training on the patient data. The encrypted model updates are sent to the central aggregation server which uses the Federated Averaging algorithm. Noise injection and gradient clipping are applied in order to enhance privacy with the help of differential privacy. There are reduced risks of information leakage through this strategy. Besides, the framework employs weighted aggregation and data augmentation to manage non-IID data distributions. In addition, explainability through Grad-Cam is added to improve clinical transparency and trust by providing the visual understanding of model predictions. This method according to the experimental results preserves a small accuracy loss to enhance privacy with an accuracy of 93.3 in centrally managed environments, 92.1 in federated learning, and 90.8 with different privacy. This is a safe and easy-to-use method and suitable in real healthcare facilities.

title: Think Through Uncertainty: Improving Long-Form Generation Factuality via Reasoning Calibration
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often hallucinate in long-form generation. Existing approaches mainly improve factuality through post-hoc revision or reinforcement learning (RL) with correctness-based rewards, but they do not teach the model to estimate which parts of its generation are reliable. As a result, models may still state incorrect claims confidently in their responses. Recent advances in reasoning have significantly improved LLM performance, and have been leveraged to estimate confidence by incorporating calibration into RL objectives. However, existing approaches remain limited to a single scalar confidence for the entire response, which is insufficient for long-form generation where uncertainty varies across individual claims. To mitigate this problem, we propose CURE, a framework that improves long-form factuality by teaching LLMs to reason about uncertainty at the claim level. We first introduce a Claim-Aware Reasoning Protocol, which structures outputs into atomic claims paired with explicit confidence estimates. We then develop a multi-stage training pipeline that aligns model confidence with claims' correctness and then optimizes on factuality. The resulting calibrated confidence further enables selective prediction, allowing the model to abstain from uncertain claims at inference time. Experiments on four long-form factuality benchmarks show that CURE consistently improves factual accuracy over competitive supervised and RL baselines, while maintaining factual recall. In particular, it improves claim-level accuracy by up to 39.9% on Biography generation. These gains are accompanied by improved calibration, as reflected by a 16.0% increase in AUROC on FactBench.

title: Hidden Measurement Error in LLM Pipelines Distorts Annotation, Evaluation, and Benchmarking
abstract: LLM evaluations drive which models get deployed, what safety standards get adopted, which research conclusions get published, and how projections of AI's labor-market impact get made. Yet standard confidence intervals ignore variability from judge model choice, model temperature, and prompt phrasing, producing under-coverage that worsens with more data. The omitted variance can shift results enough to reverse conclusions \citep{baumann2025llmhacking, huang2026dropping}; pipelines that fail to average over it leave the surface that ``benchmark hacking'' exploits \citep{singh2025leaderboard}. This paper decomposes LLM pipeline uncertainty into its sources, distinguishes variance that shrinks with more data from sensitivity to researcher design choices, and uses design-study projections to reduce total evaluation error (TEE). Across the demonstrations, naive standard errors are 40 - 60\% smaller than the TEE-corrected SE. Using Chatbot Arena data, we show naive 95\% CI coverage drops as $n$ grows while TEE-corrected coverage holds at 95\%, and TEE-guided pipelines restrict the benchmark gaming surface from 56 to 32 Elo ($K=27$), below the human-leaderboard baseline. We show further that a small pilot recovers honest CIs and projects which design changes most improve precision. Acting on those projections halves MMLU estimation error against the answer key at equivalent cost, and raises per-match agreement with human votes by 7.9 percentage points on Chatbot Arena.

title: **"Global Quantum Communication Infrastructure Atlas 2026: A Comprehensive 3D Visual Compendium of National Quantum Networks, Cross-Border Connections, Space-Based Systems, Investment Landscapes, and Country-Wise Readiness Assessment Across the United States, China, European Union Member States, South Korea, India, Japan, Canada, and Emerging Quantum Nations"**
abstract: ## Detailed Description of the Complete 10-Diagram Series ### Overview and Scope This comprehensive 3D diagrammatic compendium presents the most complete visual documentation of global quantum communication infrastructure as of 2026. The series of 10 three-dimensional diagrams, generated using Python's Matplotlib with `mplot3d` toolkit, systematically illustrates the worldwide deployment of quantum key distribution (QKD) networks, satellite-based quantum communication systems, cross-border quantum links, investment patterns, and comparative country readiness assessments. The diagrams are organized to provide a **progressive understanding** of the global quantum landscape: - **Macro-level investment and strategy** (Diagram 1)- **Regional integration** (Diagrams 2, 3)- **National infrastructure deep-dives** (Diagrams 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)- **Space-based systems** (Diagram 9)- **Comparative analysis** (Diagram 10) This compendium serves as an essential resource for policymakers, researchers, defense strategists, telecommunications planners, and investors seeking to understand the rapidly evolving global quantum communication ecosystem. --- ### Diagram-by-Diagram Description --- #### Part 1: Global Investment Landscape and Strategic Priorities **Diagram 1 – Global Quantum Technology Investment by Country (2025)** **Visual Elements:** This 3D bar chart presents the annual global investment in quantum technologies across leading nations. The visualization uses a dark background with color-coded bars representing different countries. **Key Data Presented:** | Rank | Country | Investment (Billion USD) | Share of Global ||------|---------|-------------------------|-----------------|| 1 | United States | $12.1 B | 36.4% || 2 | China | $8.25 B | 24.8% || 3 | Germany | $3.2 B | 9.6% || 4 | United Kingdom | $2.5 B | 7.5% || 5 | Japan | $2.1 B | 6.3% || 6 | South Korea | $1.4 B | 4.2% || 7 | India | $0.72 B | 2.2% || 8 | Canada | $0.6 B | 1.8% || 9 | France | $0.5 B | 1.5% || 10 | Other EU | $1.8 B | 5.4% | **Critical Insights:** - **Total Global Annual Investment:** $33.28 Billion- **USA-China Duopoly:** These two nations alone account for 61% of global quantum technology investment- **Strategic Orientation:** USA emphasizes private capital and computing dominance; China focuses on state-led sovereignty through communication and materials- **Investment-to-Revenue Ratio:** Approximately 17.7:1, indicating strategic long-horizon R&D rather than immediate commercial returns **Scientific Significance:** This diagram establishes the economic foundation of the global quantum race, demonstrating that quantum communication infrastructure is being built through massive, sustained government and private investment rather than market-driven demand. --- #### Part 2: European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI) **Diagram 2 – EuroQCI: European Quantum Communication Infrastructure Network** **Visual Elements:** This geographic 3D map shows the pan-European quantum network spanning 20+ countries. Nodes are color-coded by network status: lime (active major networks), cyan (participating), orange (under construction). title: Provenance-Conditioned Attention: Source-Type Gating for Epistemic Reasoning in Transformers
abstract: Standard transformer attention treats all tokens as epistemically interchangeable, computing relevance purely through semantic similarity of query and key vectors. This architectural design discards a critical signal in source-critical domains: the provenance type of the information being attended to. We introduce Provenance-Conditioned Attention (PCA), a mechanism that augments scaled dot-product attention with a learned, low-dimensional source-type gating channel. title: Automatically Expressing the Meaning of Logical Formulae in Natural Language
abstract: For as long as natural language generation (NLG) has existed, "logic-to-text" generation, i.e., NLG from mathematical logic formulae, has attracted attention due to its many potential applications, including intelligent tutoring systems, ontology verbalization, and explainable AI. This thesis investigates the question of how to build, and especially how to evaluate, systems for logic-to-text generation. Its contributions center on logic-to-text NLG, but also extend to the broader field of data-to-text NLG. Chapters 3 and 4 study generation mechanisms and input manipulations. In Chapter 3, I present LoLa, a rule-based logic-to-text generation system that produces English text from first-order logic formulae. Its main innovation lies in simplifying input formulae through logical equivalences prior to translation. Extensive evaluations using both standard automatic metrics and human judgments show that LoLa is effective at generating natural language translations of logical formulae. In Chapter 4, I turn to the question of identifying the most amenable input for a logic-to-text system. Focusing on the role of brevity, I introduce an algorithm for computing the shortest equivalents of an input formula and report automatic and human evaluations to show that manipulating input formulae actually improves output quality. However, it is unclear whether the shortest equivalent to a given formula is always the best input. Chapters 5 through 8 focus on evaluation. In Chapter 5, I conduct a meta-evaluation in which user interfaces employed in past human evaluations are assessed by user experience experts. Building on their insights, I derive recommendations for designing more effective and engaging annotation interfaces. In Chapter 6, I present a survey of human evaluations of hallucinations, investigating how these evaluations are designed. The analysis reveals several methodological shortcomings, including the frequent omission of crucial details such as annotation guidelines, user interface design, inter-annotator agreement metrics, and annotator demographics and compensation. In Chapter 7, I present the first implementation of a logic-based framework for hallucination analysis in real-world data-to-text domains, including logic-to-text, experimenting with both human and LLM annotators. The results show that applying the framework to concrete data-to-text domains is feasible, but not straightforward. Human annotators achieve only low to modest accuracies, depending on the domain. By contrast, models demonstrate potential to perform the annotation task, thereby enabling scalability. In Chapter 8, I introduce the concept of formulaicness, a measure of how strongly an output text mirrors the structural form of its input, and I propose its use as an enhancement for automatic evaluation of naturalness, again with a focus on logic-to-text NLG. The results suggest that formulaicness is a valuable addition to the automatic evaluation of naturalness, aligning well with human judgments and consistently improving the correlation of baseline metrics with human ratings. Overall, the thesis contributes to logic-to-text NLG in two main ways: by highlighting its specific challenges, such as the identification of more amenable inputs, and by taking steps to improve existing approaches to generation and evaluation. More broadly, it also offers more general insights for improving the evaluation of data-to-text NLG systems.

title: Exploring the Design and Impact of Interactive Worked Examples for Learners with Varying Prior Knowledge
abstract: Tutoring systems improve learning through tailored interventions, such as worked examples, but often suffer from the aptitude-treatment interaction effect where low prior knowledge learners benefit more. We applied the ICAP learning theory to design two new types of worked examples, Buggy (students fix bugs), and Guided (students complete missing rules), requiring varying levels of cognitive engagement, and investigated their impact on learning in a controlled experiment with 155 undergraduate students in a logic problem solving tutor. Students in the Buggy and Guided examples groups performed significantly better on the posttest than those receiving passive worked examples. Buggy problems helped high prior knowledge learners whereas Guided problems helped low prior knowledge learners. Behavior analysis showed that Buggy produced more exploration-revision cycles, while Guided led to more help-seeking and fewer errors. This research contributes to the design of interventions in logic problem solving for varied levels of learner knowledge and a novel application of behavior analysis to compare learner interactions with the tutor.

title: Orchid-Creator: An Authoring Tool Supporting LLM-Driven Interactive Narrative Creation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping interactive digital narratives (IDNs). However, creating complex interactive narratives while preserving narrative consistency remains challenging. We present Orchid‑Creator (Orchid), an LLM-based authoring tool that represents IDNs as story graphs with a card‑based interface for scene definition and conditional transitions. We evaluated Orchid in two studies: a usability study with eight authors, and a comparative study with 20 participants (authors, developers, and players) that compared Orchid to Twine and AI Dungeon. Authors reported that Orchid’s features met their needs (card‑based interface: 4.0/5; story graph: 4.38/5; variable setup: 4.5/5). Structuring narratives with Orchid was easier (M = 6.0/7, p <.01) and produced better‑structured stories (M = 5.3/7, p <.05) than the alternatives, balancing author control (M = 5.5/7) with outcome diversity (M = 5/7, p <.01) and maintaining comparable usability. Finally, a case study with an artist demonstrates Orchid’s utility for interactive art.

title: A Robust Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Lung Tumor Classification using Taguchi Optimization and Fuzzy Inference
abstract: Accurate early lung-tumor detection from computed tomography (CT) scans remains difficult due to noise, intensity variations, and borderline cases where tumor boundaries are visually ambiguous. This paper presents a hybrid deep learning framework named Adversarially Robust Taguchi-Optimized Fuzzy Convolutional Neural Network (ATF-CNN) for automated lung tumor classification. The pipeline begins with CT preprocessing for denoising and region enhancement, followed by CNN-based hierarchical feature extraction. To reduce trial-and-error tuning and improve training stability, Taguchi design of experiments is used to select robust hyperparameters efficiently. A fuzzy inference layer is then introduced to model uncertainty in deep features and to soften decision boundaries for difficult cases. In addition, adversarial training is incorporated to strengthen robustness against small input perturbations. The proposed model performs binary classification (tumor vs. non-tumor) and demonstrates strong performance in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and AUC, indicating its suitability for computer-aided diagnostic support.

title: Adversarial manipulation of CAN bus IDS
abstract: Recently, the automotive sector has experienced innovation driven by the increasing connectivity of vehicles not only with each other but also with integrated smart city systems. Due to this upgrade, the vehicle’s attack surface can extend to unexpected boundaries enabling complex attacks and providing access to a critical infrastructure’s network for government and military organizations for the "Country System". Considering the Machine Learning (ML) based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) as the target of these attacks, it’s essential to investigate the possible execution, risk, and impact of Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) attacks on the IDS performance in the most likely scenario for attackers i.e. the black-box one. Therefore, this work aims to verify the applicability of some black-box decision-based AML attacks in the Controller Area Network (CAN) bus frame detection task. The victim is a Supervised ML-based IDS (assumed to be resident in the vehicle itself) considering various Technology Transfer state-of-the-art ML models. The evasion attacks are Boundary and HopSkipJump, often exploited in image classification tasks. The results show the evasion attacks impact (in terms of weighted accuracy loss) is about 70% and it is approximately the same. However, the time needed for the attacks is profoundly different making the Boundary attack more appropriate in this context. In addition, it is possible to control the needed generation adversarial examples’ time through an hyperparameter related to some ML ensemble models. Adversarial Training (AT) proves to be a Security by Design and by Default countermeasure useful to prefer the Random Forest model.

title: Detecting Safety Violations Across Many Agent Traces
abstract: To identify safety violations, auditors often search over large sets of agent traces. This search is difficult because failures are often rare, complex, and sometimes even adversarially hidden and only detectable when multiple traces are analyzed together. These challenges arise in diverse settings such as misuse campaigns, covert sabotage, reward hacking, and prompt injection. Existing approaches struggle here for several reasons. Per-trace judges miss failures that only become visible across traces, naive agentic auditing does not scale to large trace collections, and fixed monitors are brittle to unanticipated behaviors. We introduce Meerkat, which combines clustering with agentic search to uncover violations specified in natural language. Through structured search and adaptive investigation of promising regions, Meerkat finds sparse failures without relying on seed scenarios, fixed workflows, or exhaustive enumeration. Across misuse, misalignment, and task gaming settings, Meerkat significantly improves detection of safety violations over baseline monitors, discovers widespread developer cheating on a top agent benchmark, and finds nearly 4x more examples of reward hacking on CyBench than previous audits.

title: THEIA: Learning Complete Kleene Three-Valued Logic in a Pure-Neural Modular Architecture
abstract: We present THEIA, a 2.75M-parameter modular neural architecture that learns the complete Kleene three-valued logic (K3) truth table from task data without external symbolic inference or hand-encoded K3 gate primitives. Across 5 seeds it passes all 39 K3 rules at >99% per-rule accuracy. K3 learnability is not the central finding: Transformer baselines also pass all 39 rules, and flat MLPs match THEIA on Phase-1 accuracy within 0.04pp. The contributions are two properties of the learned system. (1) Uncertainty-verdict asymmetric propagation. THEIA preserves Has-Unknown at every upstream boundary (80.0/91.1/90.8/99.7% across Arith/Order/Set/Logic vs. ~52% majority) while final-verdict decodability stays at or below a 73.4% U-vs-non-U oracle reference under linear and nonlinear probes. Activation patching on non-absorbent T->U cases flips 4,898/4,898 OR and 4,719/4,719 AND pairs across 5 seeds, ruling out residual shortcuts. (2) Reliability spectrum under discretized end-to-end training, on tasks decomposable along the engine boundaries. A mod-3 sequential composition task generalizes from 5- to 500-step evaluation at 99.96+-0.04% (5 seeds). Under identical Gumbel-softmax training, flat MLPs collapse to chance by 50 steps; a 2x2 ResMLP grid reaches >=99% on only 3/20 (config, seed) trials; a pre-LN Transformer reaches 99.24+-0.34%. Straight-through discretization prevents 0.999^500 compounding; the architectural separator is sustaining Phase-1 accuracy under Phase-3 training, where flat MLPs fail. Auxiliary: under per-architecture development defaults (not optimizer-controlled), THEIA reaches 12/12 Kleene coverage 6.5x faster than a parameter-comparable 8L Transformer; this narrows to ~3.6x with Transformer-standard tuning and 4.93x with the same recipe on both. Ratios are config-specific, not asymptotic.

title: Compiler Framework for Directional Transport in Zoned Neutral Atom Systems with AOD Assistance: A Hybrid Remote CZ Approach
abstract: We present a directional-transport (DT)-based remote CZ gate and compiler for zoned neutral-atom arrays that overcomes movement-bound entanglement limitations. Current AOD-based shuttling faces row/column non-crossing constraints, device-speed limits, and hardware-restricted range - bottlenecks for long-distance connectivity. Our approach reserves AODs for channel setup and micro-tuning while making DT the default for remote entanglement. Under antiblockade, a detuning-modulated pi-pulse sequence drives directional transport of a Rydberg excitation along a dynamic and resettable ancilla corridor, realizing a CZ gate between stationary, non-adjacent qubits. This cuts entangling-stage duration by approximately 50 to 90 percent versus AOD-only baselines and enables long-distance connectivity beyond objective-limited shuttling.

title: On-demand microwave single-photon source based on tantalum thin films
abstract: Single-photon sources are crucial for quantum information technologies. Here, we demonstrate a microwave single-photon source based on tantalum thin films, whose favorable material properties enable high-quality, stable photon emission. The antibunching behavior of the emitted radiation is revealed by second-order correlation measurements. Furthermore, traveling-wave parametric amplifiers are used as low-noise pre-amplifiers in the detection chains, substantially improving the signal-to-noise ratio and thereby greatly reducing the acquisition time required for second-order correlation measurements. These results demonstrate the viability of tantalum-based superconducting devices as reliable platforms for microwave quantum photonics.

title: Program to compare EBLF analysis of breast cancer data to Cleanlab's
abstract: Dyspnea in mechanically ventilated (MV) patients is assessed using the MV–Respiratory Distress Observation Scale (MV-RDOS), an observer-dependent tool subject to inter-rater variability. Comparing novel noninvasive measures of respiratory effort (PmusPTP) against such references produces discordant cases that cannot be unambiguously attributed to error in either method. We propose ensemble-based label filtering (EBLF), which leverages true-positive and true-negative agreement between two independently noisy methods to construct a high-confidence training set to adjudicate discordant cases.EBLF was validated using the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Dataset (n = 569; 30 features; pathology-confirmed labels). Two independent noisy label sets were simulated at error rates from 10% to 30%. A committee of five classifiers (Random Forest, XGBoost, Logistic Regression, SVM, k-NN) was trained on concordant cases using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated across majority, supermajority, and unanimity thresholds and benchmarked against Cleanlab.Applied to the Cancer Dataset, EBLF (15%/15% noise) improved accuracy from 0.851 to 0.970, sensitivity from 0.868 to 0.976, and specificity from 0.840 to 0.966. Gains were consistent across noise conditions and exceeded Cleanlab by 0.009–0.035 in accuracy. Fewer than 1.5% of cases were excluded at the supermajority threshold. Applied to 281 MV-RDOS–PmusPTP pairs from 45 MV patients, EBLF resolved 41 of 47 discordant cases. Accuracy improved from 0.808 to 0.865, with a marked specificity gain (0.875 to 0.952) and no change in sensitivity (0.585).EBLF offers a practical, computationally tractable approach for clinical monitoring studies using observer-dependent reference standards. Prospective validation with outcome endpoints is warranted.

Journal of Electronics & Information Technology, in press. doi: 10.11999/JEIT260063 Authors: PENG Juhong, ZHANG Zhi, LIU Peng, GE Wenhui, LIU Chen, LIAO Lingxin, ZHANG KaiAuthor：①School of Artificial Intelligence, HuBei University.②Key Laboratory of Intelligent Perception Systems and Security, Ministry of Education.③Wuchang Shipbuilding Industry Group Co., LtdDOI：10.11999/JEIT260063Original：https://jeit.ac.cn/cn/article/doi/10.11999/JEIT260063Correspondents: ZHANG Kai，29859491@qq.comOpen source date: April 13(th), 2026Funds: National Natural Science Foundation of China (62377009)Abstract:Objective Multimodal sentiment analysis is hindered by visual environmental noise, sentiment inconsistencies between images and texts, and imbalanced modal contributions. Treating all modalities indiscriminately allows visual noise to severely degrade model performance. Therefore, a robust mechanism to evaluate visual confidence and filter redundant noise is highly necessary. Methods A Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Model with Multi-source Knowledge guided Visual Confidence Perception (MKVP) is proposed (Fig. 1). A Multi-source Knowledge Guidance Matrix is constructed using syntactic, sentiment, and aspect-focused operators (Fig. 2). Driven by this matrix, a Visual Confidence Perception (VCP) module is designed to measure semantic affinity and dynamically suppress irrelevant visual noise (Fig. 3). Finally, a dual stream parallel interaction module facilitates deep cross-modal alignment, and a global gated mechanism dynamically adjusts modality fusion weights.Results and Discussions Extensive experiments are conducted on the MVSA-Single, MVSA-Multiple, and HFM datasets, where the proposed MKVP model consistently outperforms mainstream baseline models in terms of accuracy and F1 score (Table 3). Ablation studies clearly demonstrate the indispensable role of each component, particularly the VCP module, in filtering visual noise and improving feature quality (Table 5). Furthermore, feature space visualizations confirm that the VCP module effectively purifies semantic representations by driving data points with the same sentiment polarity to cluster distinctly (Fig. 4). Case analyses on mismatched samples further verify the model's superiority in resolving cross-modal semantic conflicts (Table 6). The evaluation of model complexity also indicates a high computational efficiency with low inference latency (Table 8).Conclusions The proposed MKVP framework effectively mitigates the issues of visual noise and sentiment inconsistency in multimodal sentiment analysis. By leveraging multi-source knowledge to guide visual confidence perception, and integrating dual-stream interaction with dynamic gated fusion, the model achieves highly robust sentiment representations. This approach provides an efficient and reliable solution for analyzing complex, noisy multimodal data in real-world social media scenarios.

title: Data Retrieval from Documents by Question-Answer Approach
abstract: In the present data-era world around us, everyone is using AI tools to reduce workload. Data retrieval and generation are one of the major benefits of AI tools. Typically, traditional data retrieval methods involve uploading documents to cloud storage and servers, which involves potential risks. Organizations, Researchers, Professors, Students, or anyone who must read and retrieve specific data from numerous documents can get help from data retrieval tools, but if the document contains sensitive information, it cannot be uploaded anywhere. This project aims to showcase a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application that enhances the capabilities of a Large Language Model (LLM) by integrating an external knowledge base. An automatic system that combines security and accessibility for data search and retrieval remotely in their system. Our approach is built on the idea of one-time embedding of the entire document and saving it in a local database, a paradigm shift in how we handle sensitive data. New documents can be added or removed from the database, thus decreasing data exposure. From there, these files can be queried like any other database, allowing users to query unique information regarding their questions. The query-based retrieval system returns only the data requested, without a requirement to save or aggregate any extra data. The data privacy is kept, and the retrieval process becomes much faster. Secured operation is a core principle in our system. All the data processing and retrieval activities are done in Colab runtime, thus no need to upload data in an untrusted cloud environment, contributing towards a greater sense of security and privacy surrounding privileged information. The model is completely in the colab runtime environment or local runtime environment, no data will be saved after the runtime ends, and no data will accidentally leak into the internet, risking a potential online data breach and unauthorized access. This helps securely view desired parts of the confidential information without going through all documents. With the power of LLM, the system generates the most suitable response by understanding the query statements and retrieving data from the database. Our solutions allow for private, efficient, and privacy-preserving storage of sensitive documents; query-based data retrieval to the content plus working in google colab runtime or running the notebook locally. An emergent system that could speed up looking into data and help with efficient responses.

title: "Hey Human, Why Are You So Mad At Me?": Typologizing anger expression toward LLMs and understanding its role in downstream trust and continuation decisions
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used across diverse contexts, and some users perceive them not merely as tools but as assistants or collaborators. However, repeated expectation violations can induce negative affect such as anger, disappointment, and frustration, which may degrade trust and lead to eventual discontinuation. Prior research has largely treated negative affect as an outcome and focused on mitigation, leaving underexplored how anger is processed, why users respond differently to the same violations, and how these differences shape interaction. Using a mixed-methods approach combining surveys (n = 102) and in-depth interviews (n = 17), this study identifies a typology of anger expression and examines emotional–behavioral dynamics following expectation violations during LLM use. Quantitative analyses revealed differences between users who expressed anger and those who suppressed it in emotional relief, trust, and continuation intention. Qualitative analyses indicated that these differences stem from expectations, interaction context, and perceived costs of expression rather than fixed personal traits. This study conceptualizes anger as a regulatory mechanism shaping interaction rather than as a singular emotional reaction. We highlight limitations of non-adaptive conversational LLMs and provide theoretical and empirical foundations for interactionally adaptive LLM design that can calibrate responses to users’ emotions and interaction needs.
